column1: # Cardfight!! Vanguard Dear Days 2 (Lancarse's own engine, SDK 17.5.3, update 1.7.2). Started from porter's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and checked by hand

# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main sets a heap. nninitStartup asks for the pool − used memory, SetHeapSize 0xb9400000 (2.89 GB, read on
# Android); the provisional 4.375 GB alias region left a 128 MB heap region and the game aborted there (0xd401). The heap check's rule (profile_guess.heap_signals):
# the request rounded up to 128 MB (3 GB heap region), the alias region the rest of the 5 GB block (1.5 GB: the SDK's ~1 GB node area and 512 MB)
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource

column1: # The game sets COMPRESSIBLE on every texture and fills its textures from the CPU in CPU-uncached pools, with no flush: its BC7 font arrays (1024x1024, 4 to 18 layers) after
# making them, its UI label atlas (1024x512 RGBA8; the card data screen's "Activated Ability" tabs) before. Their GPU copies stayed zeros (texture dumps on the Odin 2) while
# guest memory held them: no text anywhere, and dark corners on the card data boxes. tex_cpu_uncached takes the data in both cases (gfx_vk_tex.c, hle_nvn.c)
# The game presents at interval 1 (60 fps on the Switch) and steps by the time that really passed: its frame loop (main+0x40d120) adds the time since its last call to an
# accumulator of frames and runs as many fixed updates as it holds. Its boot screens changed every 3.0 s at 60 and at 30 fps alike (screen recordings on the Odin 2).
# 30 fps by default, half the work of 60; porter's --fps60 lifts the ceiling
